goal.f.title: Goal
goal.state.redefined: Metric definition changed: set a new baseline and target
goals.sub: Each goal compares its metric's start value with the latest measurement. "On track" means progress is keeping pace with the time elapsed toward the due date.
barber.overdue_sub: This barber's overdue regulars, most valuable first.
risk.rebuild: Rebuild profiles from the latest data
risk.empty: No clients match. If this is empty because nobody has a phone on file, tick “include clients we can't call”.
risk.ab: Optional A/B test — randomly assign one of:
offer.free_addon: Free head massage with the next haircut
outreach.sub: A case counts as won back when the client completes a visit within 60 days of the call. Revenue recovered is that visit's service price.
outreach.sync_help: Pulls the admin's outcomes, marks returned clients, sends approved cases, archives closed ones.
context.sub: Context is the second source of truth next to the facts: what was going on and how analysis should take it into account. A factor has a period (days or weeks), a scope, may recur every year, and may carry a belief about its effect.
hyp.sub: Test whether a change moved a metric. "Compare with a control group" uses difference-in-differences on weekly values: the change in the barbers you changed something for, minus the change in barbers you didn't. The 95% interval shows how sure the result is; if it crosses zero, the effect is not proven.
hyp.title_ph: Rebooking at checkout raises the return rate
hyp.statement_ph: What changed, and what you expect to happen
verdict.not_enough_weeks: Not enough weeks of data to evaluate.
verdict.not_enough_control: Not enough control weeks to evaluate.
verdict.did_unclear: No clear effect on {metric}: {effect} (95% CI {lo} to {hi})
verdict.ab_need_10: Need at least 10 closed cases per offer.
verdict.ab_need_two: Needs exactly two offers with closed cases.
playbook.sub: Routines the team agrees to use. Each tip shows on the pages of the barbers it applies to.
data.sub: Data comes in through files Claude fetches from the Altegio Pro connector and the client export from Altegio. Ask Claude to “refresh the barber goals” for the monthly routine.
data.save_sub: Computes every metric for every barber and the team over whole weeks and stores it, so goals move. Use the weeks since the last measurement.
data.label: Label
flash.proposed: Proposed {n} cases. Review them below, then approve.

flash.sheet_missing: The Google Sheet is not set up yet: see README, “Admin call sheet”.

treatment.suppress_overdue: do not treat the client as overdue
lens.title: Lenses
lens.sub: A lens is a rule for which factor treatments a calculation honours. Every analysis run stores the factors its lens resolved to. For now only the barber scorecard honours a lens.

report.sec.factors: What was in force in this period

risk.sub_short: Who has been away and who is worth a call. Most valuable first.
risk.how_lead: Counted from the date of the last visit. A client's usual gap is the typical time between their own visits, not one number for everyone.
risk.how_slipping: Past the usual gap, but nowhere near overdue yet.
risk.how_overdue: Silent longer than max({min} days, {factor} × usual gap) — and no more than {lapsed} days.
risk.how_one_time: Came once and has not returned for over {min} days.
risk.how_switched: Within the usual gap, but the last cut was not with their usual barber.
risk.how_example: Example: a usual gap of {ex_gap} days → overdue after {ex_line} days of silence. First-timers have no usual gap yet, so only the {min}-day rule applies to them.
